Most AI strategies fail at portfolio level: hundreds of use-case ideas, no value discipline, no owner for the controls. We run a six-week Value Mapping Sprint that scores candidate use cases on value density, data readiness, regulatory exposure and operational absorption, then sequences a 24-month roadmap with funding gates tied to measured outcomes rather than delivery milestones.

The output is an operating blueprint: named executive owner per use case, named control owner per model, an architecture baseline, a build-buy-partner decision per layer, and a value case per initiative stated in the CFO's units — contribution margin, loss rate, working capital, or headcount redeployment.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
